---
title: Vue SFC
icon: PanelsTopLeft
description: Read compiled Vue 3 components as templates and setup code.
---

Compiled Vue components can hide a simple template behind a wall of render
calls. With `--vue-sfc`, Wakaru can recover a readable `.vue` file so you
can follow the component's structure, state, and event handlers.

This is experimental Vue 3 recovery. The result helps you understand the
component; it does not recreate the original source file.

## Recover a component

```bash
mkdir -p out
npx wakaru component.js --vue-sfc -o out/component.js
```

Wakaru writes decompiled JavaScript and, when recovery succeeds, a `.vue`
file alongside it:

```text
out/
├── component.js
└── component.vue
```

Open the `.vue` file to read the component. Keep the JavaScript nearby to
check anything that looks incomplete or unclear.

## Read the recovered component

The `<template>` brings elements, bindings, conditions, and loops back into
view. The `<script setup>` brings together state and logic such as props,
refs, computed values, and event handlers.

In this example, the recovered template makes it easy to spot a list and
its insert, reset, shuffle, and remove buttons. You can follow each
`@click` to the function that changes the list:

![Playground with Vue SFC on: compiled render function on the left, recovered script setup and template on the right](/screenshots/vue-sfc.png)

[Try the Vue list transition example in the playground][vue-example].

Styles, comments, and custom SFC blocks are not recovered. Names depend on
what survived compilation, and imports or complex template patterns may
still need work. Review the result before trying to use it in an application.

## Recover components from a bundle

```bash
npx wakaru bundle.js --unpack --vue-sfc -o out/
```

Every unpacked module still gets a JavaScript file. Modules that recover as
Vue components also get a sibling `.vue` file. You can browse the recovered
components without losing the rest of the application's code.

See [Unpack a bundle](/guides/unpack-a-bundle) for working with multiple
files or chunks.

## Checking what happened

If no `.vue` file appears, use the JavaScript output to inspect the
component. Some compiled patterns are not yet supported.

With `--unpack`, add `--json` to check each module's recovery status:

- `recovered_vue_sfc`: a `.vue` artifact was written
- `vue_sfc_source_js`: the paired JavaScript for a recovered module
- `vue_sfc_fallback_js`: the module looked like Vue but stayed JavaScript

If you only want the recovered Vue file, use `-o App.vue`. This makes the
command fail when recovery is not possible. See the
[CLI reference](/reference/cli#vue-sfc-recovery-experimental) for the output options.
